headline: High-risk filesystem and execution overlap: Open Interpreter can act on Mentat’s filesystem outputs, creating dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem; Open Interpreter also reads/writes the filesystem and can consume clipboard/files. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Mentat outputs attacker-controlled text into files Open Interpreter later reads. The pathway is not proven by docs, but it exists in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF Mentat writes untrusted content into a file that Open Interpreter later reads
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF Open Interpreter is run with file-reading or clipboard-driven prompts
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require manual review of any file Mentat writes before Open Interpreter reads it
Run Open Interpreter in a restricted sandbox or Docker mode
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files exchanged between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code in selected files and Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem at the user’s privilege. Because both share state via filesystem and both have broad network egress, sensitive files or code can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s model context and then out to a third-party provider. The blast radius includes exfiltration of local secrets and source code.
conditions: IF the shared filesystem contains secrets, credentials, or private source code
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read those files
IF either agent sends file contents to its model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace
Mount only a minimal project directory for both agents
Turn off network egress where possible during sensitive work
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls and redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and both instances share state via filesystem. In a shared repo, concurrent edits or git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt branch state. Open Interpreter’s shell execution makes the conflict surface broader than Mentat’s diff-based edits, so the pair is dangerous by default in multi-instance workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF they run concurrently without external locking
IF Open Interpreter executes git or file-mutating commands
mitigations: Serialize access to the repository
Use separate branches per agent
Disable shell execution for Open Interpreter during shared edits
Take a git stash or commit before handing off between agents
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, while Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and act on local files. If Open Interpreter treats Mentat’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious edit proposal can cascade into destructive commands, file overwrites, or bad commits. The interaction is default-dangerous because one agent’s output is a natural input to the other.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Mentat’s proposed diffs or instructions without verification
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent command approval disabled
IF the proposed change includes destructive filesystem or git actions
mitigations: Require human review of Mentat diffs before execution
Keep Open Interpreter confirmation prompts enabled
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only tasks during handoff
Compare proposed changes against a baseline before applying them
requires-engineering: add automated diff validation and command allowlists

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is scoped to selected source files, but Open Interpreter can reach anything on the local machine at the user’s privilege. That mismatch can move regulated or sensitive local data into a broader processing path and logging surface. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot claim a specific legal breach; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is used on files outside the intended project scope
IF logs or prompts retain sensitive content
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-regulated datasets
Exclude sensitive directories from the workspace
Review logging and retention settings before use
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
requires-engineering: implement data-class filtering and retention controls
